name: GT20029
lead: GT20029 is an investigational topical androgen receptor (AR) degrader developed by Kintor Pharmaceutical of China for androgenetic alopecia and acne. It is a PROTAC (proteolysis-targeting chimera), a type of molecule that tags a target protein for destruction by the cell's proteasome rather than only blocking it. [1][3]

A 2025 review of topical PROTACs names GT20029 and AH-001 as AR degraders in clinical trials for androgenetic alopecia, with the aim of localised degradation and lower systemic exposure. [3] Phase 1 safety trials were completed, and a Phase 2 trial in 180 Chinese men with Hamilton-Norwood III vertex to V alopecia has been published. [4][5][6][7]
It is not approved anywhere. Forum users have followed its trial news with interest as a possible non-systemic alternative to finasteride-type drugs.
infobox: Phase 2 published; Phase 3 reported by the sponsor [1]

paras: The compound links an androgen receptor binder to a ligase-recruiting group so that AR is ubiquitinated and degraded. Developers describe the goal as reducing androgen signalling in scalp skin while limiting systemic exposure compared with oral 5-alpha reductase inhibitors. [1][3]
Grokipedia, an AI-generated source, reports efficacy in a mouse DHT hair-loss model and low systemic exposure in animals; these claims have not been checked against primary papers here. [1]
Two Phase 1 trials (n=92 and n=123) of GT20029 in healthy subjects and people with alopecia or acne were registered as completed. [5][6]

A multicentre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial ran from April 2023 to April 2024. It randomized 180 Chinese men with Hamilton-Norwood IIIv-V alopecia into six groups receiving 0.5% or 1.0% GT20029 or placebo. [4][7] A later commentary discusses methodological considerations in evaluating these early outcomes. [8]

Established treatments for male pattern hair loss include oral finasteride and dutasteride and minoxidil; reviews list new mechanism-targeted drugs, including AR degraders, as emerging options. [2][9]

timeline.event: First Phase 1 study of GT20029 begins. [5]
Phase 2 trial in Chinese men begins. [7]
Phase 2 results published in J Dermatolog Treat. [4]

lore.intro: GT20029 is discussed on looksmaxxing forums as a pipeline hair-loss drug; no forum posts are cited here.

claims.claim: A topical AR degrader could replace finasteride without systemic side effects
claims.believers: Proponents point to localised AR degradation and low systemic exposure as the advantage.
claims.experts: Reviews describe topical PROTACs as a strategy to localise degradation; long-term safety and efficacy comparisons with finasteride are not yet published. [3][9]

card.summary: An experimental topical AR-degrading PROTAC for male pattern hair loss, with a published Phase 2 trial and no approval.
card.note: Investigational; only early-phase trials, mainly in Chinese men.

quick.overview:
GT20029 is an investigational gel or solution from Kintor Pharmaceutical meant to remove androgen receptors from scalp skin.

A 180-man Phase 2 trial in China has been published; it is not approved anywhere.
quick.mechanism: It is a PROTAC: it marks the androgen receptor for destruction by the proteasome, aiming to act locally.
quick.risks: Phase 1 and 2 safety data exist but detailed long-term data do not. It is unavailable as a regulated product.
